summary: Recent discussions focus on SPIP, a language‑agnostic UDF protocol, and its external lookup join extension, a fallback resolver for unknown V2 catalog names, and a trial of automated AI code review for new pull requests. These threads illustrate ongoing efforts to improve Spark's extensibility, catalog handling, and code quality automation.

highlights.text: SPIP proposes a unified API and execution protocol for user‑defined functions that can run outside the Spark engine via IPC, enabling consistent support across multiple languages.

sources.title: SPIP: Language-agnostic UDF Protocol for Spark

highlights.text: SPIP also introduces an external lookup join strategy that queries external storage on demand, avoiding the need to materialize the static side before joining.
A fallback resolver for unknown V2 catalog names will be consulted when an application references a V2 catalog name that has not been pre‑configured in Spark.

sources.title: [DISCUSS][SQL] SPARK-59849: Fallback resolver for unknown V2 catalog names

highlights.text: A trial of automated AI code review using Claude was launched for new Apache Spark pull requests, posting only advisory comments without approvals.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] Automated AI code review on new Spark PRs (trial)
